main_body: Thatched-roof hut: a large sloped thatch roof (rows 5-54) over a log-palisade front wall with a central door (rows 55-78)
top_band: ochre thatch roof slope, rows 7-50 (L 95-154, layered tile courses), widening toward the eave; it is clearly lighter than the dark log wall below
evidence: The roof is drawn as a big sloped surface seen from above. Its silhouette widens down to overhanging eaves with stepped sides, and the dark log wall sits below it. This matches the Beodeul reference houses, whose roofs also read as top slopes above the wall. A dark shadow row sits under the eave at about row 55. The door has a timber frame, an inner dark opening and a stone threshold, so it reads as inset. The log wall with its two round shields is a vertical south face. There is no receding side face.

style.evidence: The thatch uses about 6 steps (dark brown, mid, base, light, highlight), with a dark course line under each row and a light speckle per course. The logs have several brown tones with grain and the shields have rings. Outlines are dark brown, with only 13% neutral edge pixels. Median colours per tile (9) are close to house-h112 (11) but below h101 (18), and total colours (38) are lower than both references. The thatch courses are quite regular and repetitive, but flat-fill coverage is only 2%. It would sit acceptably next to the references.
